newsitem.title: THAILAND: GOLF-TIGER WOODS CLINCHES CLASSIC TITLE BY 10 SHOTS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER WOODS CLINCHES CLASSIC TITLE BY 10 SHOTS.

text.p: American Tiger Woods won his fourth title since turning professional last August with an emphatic 10-stroke victory in the Bangkok Classic on Sunday.
The 21-year-old fired a final round 68 for a 20-under total of 268 in only his 12th professional appearance to win the $300,000 tournament at the Thai Country Club.

South Korea's Joong-Kyung Mo shot 68 to take second place. Canada's Jim Rutledge fired a brilliant 63 to grab a share of third place on 279 with Carlos Expinoza of Mexico and Tse-Peng Chang of Taiwan.
Woods came close to not starting the tournament after suffering from heat exhaustion during a pro-am here on Wednesday. He withdrew after the 13th hole as temperatures soared to 33 degrees Celsius.
Woods, a local favourite because of his Thai mother, has attracted huge crowds during the Bangkok Classic -- his first as a professional in Asia.
His arrival in Bangkok received live television coverage and dozens of excited fans greeted their "native son" at the airport.
